newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ CPI risks going negative without govt charges.
newsitem.headline: NZ CPI risks going negative without govt charges.

text.p: The Manufacturers Federation said on Tuesday that CPI inflation in New Zealand was at risk of going negative if government and local body charges were removed from calculations.
"Increased government charges, both central and local, accounted for 70 percent of the increase in quarter to June," ManFed chief executive Simon Arnold said.
"For the year to June these government price hikes were two fifths of the inflation of 1.1 percent.
"If government costs are taken out, inflation is now at risk of going negative, outside the Reserve Bank's (0-3 percent) target band," he said.
The Reserve Bank estimated underlying inflation, which it uses as the measure for assessing whether it meets its target, was 1.5 percent in the June year.
